title: Sum an arbitrary number of numeric arguments
description: Write a function called add_all_nums which takes arbitrary number of arguments and sums all the arguments. Check if all the list items are number types. If not do give a reasonable feedback.
examples:
>>> add_all_nums(1, 2, 3)
6
>>> add_all_nums(1, 2, 'three')
'All arguments must be numbers.'
hints: *args collects any number of positional arguments into a tuple.
Use isinstance(x, (int, float)) together with all() to check every argument is a number.
If not all(...) is True, return a feedback string like 'All arguments must be numbers.' instead of summing.
expected_behavior: Returns the sum of all arguments if every argument is an int or float; otherwise returns a feedback string explaining the problem.
explanation: *args gathers the arguments into a tuple. all(isinstance(x, (int, float)) for x in args) verifies every item is numeric before summing; if any item fails that check, a feedback string is returned instead of attempting the sum.
